candidates.exact_span: Stream segment specific (20.6.4.401 NMAC) WQS for pH, 6.6 to 9.0 standard units (s.u.), are more restrictive than the technology-based limits presented earlier
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes the water-quality-based numeric pH range (6.6–9.0 s.u.) that would supersede technology-based limits for compliance comparison; a different reading of restrictiveness or segment applicability would change which pH limit is enforceable.

candidates.exact_span: The pH limits of 6.6 to 9.0 s.u. in the previous permit, which are protective of the downstream Navajo Nation standards, will be continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States that 6.6–9.0 s.u. limits carry forward into the draft permit; interpreting 'continued' as operative versus provisional could change whether these values are the applicable enforceable limits during FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: Primary contact currently is one of the designated uses of State of New Mexico Segment No. 20.6.4.401 of the San Juan basin.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Designated-use classification determines which WQS criteria govern the discharge; a different interpretation of the segment's designated uses would change which numeric bacteria limits apply.

candidates.exact_span: The State of New Mexico WQS criteria applicable to the primary contact designated use of the receiving stream are the monthly geometric mean of E. coli bacteria of 126 cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL) and single sample of 410 cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies enforceable concentration limits (126 geometric mean; 410 single sample) tied to primary contact; alternate readings of designated-use applicability or limit type (geometric mean vs single sample) would change which threshold is used for each measurement.

candidates.exact_span: The results for E. coli may be reported as either colony forming units (CFU) or the most probable number (MPN) depending on the analytical method used.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether CFU and MPN are treated as directly comparable to the stated cfu/100 mL (or MPN/100 mL) limits affects whether a reported value can be matched to an enforceable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: The E. coli daily mass loading limit of 3.19 x 1010 cfu/day in the TMDL was established
candidates.computation_change_reason: Introduces a mass-loading (cfu/day) limit distinct from concentration limits; whether this limit is operative for the discharge would change which numeric standard applies and how reported loads are evaluated.

candidates.exact_span: Daily mass loading limit, cfu/day = C, cfu/100 mL * 1,000 mL/L * l/0.264 gallons * Q, flow, expressed in 1,000,000 gallons/day
candidates.computation_change_reason: The conversion formula governs derivation of the mass-loading limit from concentration and flow; different interpretation of units or formula terms would change the computed enforceable loading cap.

candidates.exact_span: C = state water quality standard criterion for bacteria, 126 cfu/100 mL
candidates.computation_change_reason: Fixes the concentration input (C) used to derive the daily mass-loading limit; a different reading of which criterion value applies would change the resulting loading limit.

candidates.exact_span: Q = stream flow in million gallons per day (mgd), 299 MGD
candidates.computation_change_reason: Fixes the flow input (Q) used to derive the daily mass-loading limit; a different interpretation of applicable receiving-stream flow would change the computed loading limit.

candidates.exact_span: Downstream Navajo Nation segment specific WQS for E. coli bacteria are 126 cfu/100 mL monthly geometric mean for domestic water supply, and 235 cfu/100 mL to 575 cfu/100 mL single sample maximum for secondary human contact.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets alternative downstream numeric criteria (including 235 cfu/100 mL single-sample maximum) that may be more stringent than NM primary-contact limits; interpretation of which downstream use/standard is controlling would change applicable limits.

candidates.exact_span: The E. coli monthly geometric mean limit of 126 cfu/100 mL, daily maximum limit of 235 cfu/100 mL and daily maximum mass loading limit of 3.19 x 1010 cfu/day in the previous permit will be continued in the draft permit to be consistent with the New Mexico TMDL and protective of the more stringent NNWQS.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Consolidates three continued enforceable limits (126 geometric mean, 235 daily maximum concentration, 3.19×10¹⁰ cfu/day mass loading) and resolves tension with the earlier 410 cfu/100 mL single-sample criterion; different readings of which limits are actually carried forward would change compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: The E. coli monitoring frequency requirement in the previous permit be also continued in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: References a monitoring-frequency obligation carried from the prior permit; whether and how that frequency applies determines required monitoring (Purpose B) and whether absent results represent missing required evidence versus an unrequired period (Purpose C).
